correctness.rationale: Represent 3n=(3k+1)x+(3k+2)y with x≡y mod3 to obtain generators m=2k+1,u=3k+1,v=3k+2. Minimality follows m<u<v<2m. Since u+v=3m and u≡k,v≡-k modm, the Apéry set is W_j=min(ju,(m-j)v), j=0..2k, split at j=k; ±1 neighbors shift j by ∓2. Only j=k (h=1) and j=k+1 (h=1,2) satisfy both neighbor inequalities. Sum W_j proves genus; max W_j proves Frobenius. The k=1 boundary has gaps {1,2}, none isolated. Independently constructed coin-membership DP and direct quotient checks passed 49,345 bounded assertions over k<=140; unrestricted proof is the Apéry argument.

value.rationale: Isolated gaps are a standard natural invariant related to perfect numerical semigroups. The threefold quotients of consecutive coprime generators are a canonical, infinite embedding-dimension-three family; a complete three-point isolation pattern and exact boundary at k=1 is an unknown, non-implied classification beyond the contextual genus/Frobenius and generic Apéry algorithm, potentially useful as test family for isolation and quotient theory.
